seed: Objects of type `chaser` under action ACTION5 with touching neighbours [block,wall] show mixed outcomes: x x1, y x1. Find the condition in the before state that decides the outcome. Start from this kind of condition: the presence, type or relative position of a neighbouring object. Verify it against every transition before you keep it.

synth.notes:
Player: A1-4 turn cap and move 4 unless blocked by wall/box/chaser/bounds; the box in front gets the faced tag; A5 toggles faced<->grabbed; a grabbed box moves with the player.
Chaser acts every step: release a seated carried box > pick up a touching idle box > step 4 toward the nearest pickup point (box.x+4,box.y), or toward the nearest empty slot+4 when carrying.
The chaser tries x first and moves on y only when x is blocked (by a seated box) or already equal. That explains the mixed x/y outcomes under A5 (t19 x reached, t13/t27 blocked by a seated box).
A carried box rides at chaser.x-4 and seats on an exact empty-slot hit. Boxes are renamed by (y,x). Wall pixels = dither pattern with higher-layer objects occluding it. Boxes pass through the wall.
Unconfirmed: pulling/turning while grabbed, chaser-player collisions, chaser crossing the wall, what happens when all slots are filled. Passes stateless (no hidden state).
